## Issue #1017 CI/CD False Positives, False Negatives, Warnings And Errors

Issue [#1017](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1017) requires
the non-passing default-branch run to be fixed at its root cause, and every
false positive, false negative, warning and error in CI/CD to be found,
classified and corrected — using the current Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript and
Python pipeline templates and the Hive Mind CI/CD guidance as the comparison
baseline, and delivering everything in the single prepared pull request.

The run named by the issue reported `CI/CD Pipeline` as `cancelled` and
`Desktop Release` as `skipped`. The reconstruction shows why: a macOS core
slice spent 133 seconds on unbudgeted setup before starting a step whose
480-second budget would have expired 1.3 seconds *after* the job's own
600-second `timeout-minutes` cap. The runner therefore always won the race, and
GitHub reports a `timeout-minutes` kill as `cancelled` rather than `failed` —
the same class of false negative as issue #977, one level down. The general
rule this issue establishes is that **`timeout-minutes` is a backstop, never
the deadline**.

| ID | Requirement | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1017-1 | Fix the non-passing default-branch run at its root cause rather than by raising the cap that hid it. | `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh` now terminates the command's process group at its deadline and exits 124 with an `::error`, so an overrun reports `failure`; `.github/workflows/macos-core-tests.yml` runs 16 slices with a 600s budget under a 900s cap. |
| R1017-2 | Make "the step budget expires before the job clock it sits under" a checked invariant across every workflow, not a per-job accident. | `MAX_BUDGET_SHARE_PERCENT = 70` in `tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1017.rs`; `every_step_budget_expires_before_the_job_clock_it_guards` and `every_job_declares_a_timeout_or_delegates_to_one_that_does` sweep every job of every workflow. |
| R1017-3 | Classify every annotation and every warning- or error-shaped line in the collected logs, fix each defect, and state why each remaining diagnostic is kept. | The ledger in `dev/log/issues/1017/pulls/1018/README.md` §4: twelve fixed defects and seven dispositioned classes, sourced from `annotations/all-annotations.tsv` and `analysis/soft-warnings.txt`. |
| R1017-4 | Remove the security false negatives: no `cargo audit` ran on the default branch, and a CodeQL run reported success while 1,023 live source files were extracted with errors. | A `cargo-audit` job in `.github/workflows/security.yml` including on the weekly `schedule:`, and the extractor sysroot pin required by `github/codeql#19982`, pinned by `every_ignored_advisory_carries_a_proof_that_ci_rechecks` and `codeql_rust_lane_pins_the_extractor_sysroot`. |
| R1017-5 | Remove the security false positive without creating a permanent blind spot. | `.cargo/audit.toml` ignores RUSTSEC-2026-0235 with a machine-checkable proof line that `scripts/check-rust-dependencies.sh` re-derives from `cargo tree --invert` on every run, so the ignore expires by itself once the crate becomes reachable. |
| R1017-6 | Stop diagnostics that a run's own cancellation manufactures, and test the parsers those diagnostics come from. | `.github/workflows/links.yml` uses `!cancelled()` instead of `always()` for the broken-link error, and runs `scripts/check-web-archive.test.mjs` before lychee. |
| R1017-7 | Put every read-only job in a concurrency group so a superseded push releases its runners, without ever cancelling the default branch. | `superseded_read_only_work_releases_its_runners` sweeps every job in every workflow and forces each exemption to be argued in the test rather than left implicit in the YAML. |
| R1017-8 | Compare the complete file tree against all three pipeline templates and the Hive Mind guidance, adopt the applicable practices, and state each deviation explicitly. | `dev/log/issues/1017/pulls/1018/README.md` §5, with `analysis/template-diffs/` and immutable template copies under `references/templates/`. |
| R1017-9 | Report the shared and upstream defects with reproductions, workarounds and code-level fix suggestions. | Five exact report bodies in `dev/log/issues/1017/pulls/1018/upstream-reports/`, each recording the URL it was filed under: the missing step-execution budget in each of the three templates ([rust#135](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/135), [js#137](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/137), [python#60](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/60)), and a repository-scale data point for `github/codeql#19982` ([comment 5309221141](https://github.com/github/codeql/issues/19982#issuecomment-5309221141)) with a follow-up carrying the measured before/after counts ([comment 5309264165](https://github.com/github/codeql/issues/19982#issuecomment-5309264165)). |
| R1017-10 | Add debug output and a verbose mode where the evidence was insufficient, defaulting to off. | Three, each off by default: the `FORMAL_AI_CI_VERBOSE` heartbeat in `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh`, pinned off-by-default by `budget_wrapper_heartbeat_is_available_but_off_by_default`; `FORMAL_AI_TRACE_SLOW_INIT`, which reports each whole-source parse with its byte count and duration; and `FORMAL_AI_TRACE_COMMANDS`, which reports a spawned command's resolved path, budget, elapsed time and whether the deadline fired. |
| R1017-11 | Apply every fix everywhere the defect occurs, not only where it was observed. | Each fix is pinned by a repository-wide sweep; the sweeps found two further instances the incident never touched — a job at 1415s of a 1500s cap and a job with no `timeout-minutes` at all. The agent-sandbox fix exists in two places and was applied to both: `src/agent.rs` and its `tests/source/agent.rs` mirror. |
| R1017-12 | Retain the collected evidence in the repository so every claim can be re-derived without GitHub access, and deliver the whole change in the single prepared pull request. | `dev/log/issues/1017/pulls/1018/`, the issue and pull-request case studies, the changelog fragment, and pull request #1018. |

## Issue #1021 Full-Range Coding And Contribution Artifacts

Issue [#1021](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1021) collects
the prompts Formal AI answered wrongly, the capabilities a contribution needs to
land, and the demand that the whole loop be test-covered in one pull request.
See PR #1027 and `docs/case-studies/issue-1021/`.

The rule the issue states first governs every row below: "solve by
generalization, not specialization -- a per-prompt fix that makes one task pass
is a regression against that instruction, not progress". Rows marked **not
delivered** are reported rather than quietly narrowed, per the issue's own "the
bar is not to be met by lowering it".

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1021-1 | Deliver every sub-issue in a single pull request rather than as a backlog. | One branch, one pull request, one composed body that closes #1021. |
| R1021-2 | Fix the rule that was wrong, never the prompt that exposed it. | Every routing change lands in a rule with its vocabulary in `data/seed/`, and each is pinned by held-out paraphrases in `tests/unit/issue_1021_behaviour_range.rs`. |
| R1021-3 | #868: a bare `ls` is the request, not a fragment. | `bare_shell_tokens` reads the terminal-command catalog, so an argument-free command routes to `exec_command` (`a_bare_command_is_the_request`). |
| R1021-4 | #866/#867: `Execute ls command` runs `ls`, not `ls command`. | The command-naming noun is declared per language in `data/seed/terminal-commands.lino` and stripped before the passthrough (`a_command_naming_noun_is_not_an_argument`). |
| R1021-5 | #865: `List me files here` lists files; `Hello` still greets. | `src/agentic_coding/directory_listing.rs` composes a listing request from seeded parts in any word order (`a_prose_listing_request_routes_to_ls_in_any_word_order`). The detector is never told which language it is reading, so adding a `language es` block to `data/seed/shell-intents.lino` routed four held-out Spanish word orders with no Rust change -- finding 11 of the case study. |
| R1021-6 | #863: an example request for copy stdin to stdout in Rust is answered with code. | `copy_stdin_to_stdout` is a catalogued task like any other, with a verified template in each of the thirteen catalogued languages, so the reported prompt and held-out paraphrases in five natural languages are answered with code (`a_named_exercise_is_answered_as_a_program`) and the `cp stdin stdout` misrouting is gone with it (`a_named_exercise_is_not_a_file_operation`). A task that consumes input carries the input it was verified against into its run command (`the_stdin_answer_prints_the_input_it_was_verified_against`); one that reads nothing keeps its plain run command (`a_task_that_reads_no_input_keeps_its_plain_run_command`). |
| R1021-7 | #862: a Rosetta Code URL is a task to solve, not a `cp` operand. | The URL is no longer lowered to `cp`, and the exercise it names is solved: `Execute https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Copy_stdin_to_stdout in Rust` reaches the same catalogued task as the prose that names it, and is answered with the same verified program (`a_named_exercise_is_not_a_file_operation`, `a_named_exercise_is_answered_as_a_program`). |
| R1021-8 | #723: a request naming PHP Laravel is answered in Laravel, not in PHP-in-general. | The catalog's language axis is an *implementation-target* axis: a row may be a framework of another row (`ProgramLanguage::framework_of`), and a request naming both resolves to the more specific one. Laravel is a target of its own -- its own template, file path, check command and run command (`a_framework_named_coding_request_is_answered_in_that_framework`, `every_framework_target_carries_its_own_execution_surface`) -- while composing a program out of catalogued idioms still reads the base language through `base_language`, because Laravel adds no way of sorting a list that PHP does not have. PHP itself joins the catalog with the verified task templates every other catalogued language carries. |
| R1021-9 | #824: a filesystem move it refuses should be performed. | Operands are filtered by how a path is written rather than by where it points, so an absolute or `~`-relative move is planned (`a_move_between_absolute_paths_is_performed`). |
| R1021-10 | #943 (E91): guard against harness-created issues before any GitHub write authority. | `gh issue create` is on the never-delegated rung of `src/contribution_write_path.rs` and is refused in both opt-in states (`filing_an_issue_is_refused_in_both_states`). |
| R1021-11 | #944 (E92): rungs on the mutating-action ladder. | Delivered on both axes. The publishing rungs are refused-unless-opted-in and never-delegated (`tests/unit/issue_1021_write_path.rs`). The filesystem rungs `824.L1`-`824.L5` join the issue #916 write-effect ladder with the sandbox-reset semantics the issue asks for by name: each rung declares the state it starts from, its directory is emptied and checked to be empty, the declared state is written and then *read back off disk*, and a start that did not land is a `sandbox` violation rather than a silent premise (`experiments/issue_916_write_effect_ladder/test_ladder.py::SandboxResetTests`). All sixteen rungs are green against the real release binary and the ratchet moved 11/11 -> 16/16. |
| R1021-12 | #946 (E94): versioned recoverable memory. | `src/memory_revision.rs` captures the bytes of every tracked file *before* a candidate version is written and restores them exactly when it fails, so a self-compile that does not build leaves the workspace on the last version that did (`a_version_that_does_not_compile_leaves_the_previous_one_in_place`). The baseline that judges a version is pinned by digest, and a candidate that edits it is rolled back before its verdict is consulted (`a_candidate_that_edits_a_baseline_test_is_rolled_back_before_it_is_scored`). |
| R1021-13 | #947 (E95): bounded autonomy with a stuck-recovery limit. | `src/bounded_autonomy.rs` bounds a run on an injected clock: `RecoveryLoop::step` answers `Continue` until the limit -- one hour by default -- is spent, then presents the plan and asks (`a_loop_that_never_resolves_stops_at_the_limit_and_asks`). Per-command permission is the default mode and full trust is a separate opt-in, so delegating the commands is not delegating the choices (`full_trust_does_not_arrive_with_the_full_autonomous_mode`). |
| R1021-14 | #924 (E77): one real repository change per release landing as a normal reviewed pull request. | **Not delivered by a `solve` run**; `data/meta/self-hosting-ledger.lino` still reads `0.00% self-authored`. |
| R1021-15 | Produce the changelog fragment a code change needs. | `formal_ai::contribution_artifacts::compose` renders it from `data/seed/contribution-artifacts.lino` into the shape `scripts/check-changelog-fragment.rs` accepts. |
| R1021-16 | Produce a pull-request body that links its issue with a closing keyword. | Same generator; the closing line leads the body, and `scripts/check-pull-request-link.rs` accepts it. |
| R1021-17 | Generated code is R379-clean. | Delivered narrowly: `src/contribution_artifacts.rs` holds no natural-language literal, all wording living in seed data. It is not a claim about arbitrary future generated code. |
| R1021-18 | Pin each reported prompt as a routing test with held-out paraphrases. | `tests/unit/issue_1021_behaviour_range.rs` tests unseen word orders and languages, not the reported strings alone. |
| R1021-19 | Test the process artifacts by driving the generator, not by asserting on a fixture. | `the_committed_process_artifacts_are_generator_output` compares every committed fragment and the body against `compose` output; `examples/issue_1021_write_contribution_artifacts.rs` writes them the same way. |
| R1021-20 | Test the write path in both states, with `issue create` refused in both. | `tests/unit/issue_1021_write_path.rs` exercises both states in one process. |
| R1021-21 | Pin the closed circle as a replayable session. | `closed_circle_session_replays` compares `docs/case-studies/issue-1021/closed-circle-run/session.json` byte for byte against a fresh drive of the public API. |
| R1021-22 | Definition of done: a pull request opened by Formal AI from a real `solve` run, green without a human editing the branch. | **Not achieved.** The artifacts such a run needs are delivered and pinned; the run is the remaining gap. |
| R1021-23 | Do not meet the bar by lowering it. | No gate was relaxed. The two ratchets touched moved in the improving direction: the outside-core ceiling drops to 19,539 lines, and the seed-metadata gap floor rises only by closure-generated records. |
| R1021-24 | Collect the case-study data the standing clauses require. | `docs/case-studies/issue-1021/` holds the timeline, requirement list, per-requirement plans, library survey, online research, raw GitHub data, and probe logs. |
| R1021-25 | Add debug output wherever a root cause is not visible in existing logs. | The `examples/issue_1021_*.rs` probes, with their output preserved under `docs/case-studies/issue-1021/logs/`. |
| R1021-26 | File upstream issues with reproductions for defects that are not ours. | [openai/codex#39487](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/39487): from `@openai/codex@0.148.0` on, the ENTER answering the first-run trust dialog is dropped if it arrives as the dialog renders. Reproduced without Formal AI by `experiments/issue_1021_codex_tui_version/codex_trust_dialog_probe.py`; the bisect through the real harness is `run.sh` beside it. Every *other* root cause in this case study traced back into this repository. |
| R1021-27 | Give every requirement a traceability row. | The rows above and their entries in `docs/requirements-traceability.md`, honest "not yet confirmed" included. |
| R1021-28 | A CI failure caused by a transient upstream stall is survived, not merely reported. | `scripts/apt-install-with-retry.sh` bounds each attempt inside the step budget issue #1017 added, kills a stalled attempt while the budget still has room for another, and refuses to start when its attempts cannot fit -- so a hung package mirror can no longer fail a pull request that did not cause it. See finding 14. |
| R1021-29 | A test that reports a process was terminated distinguishes termination from a write that has not happened yet. | `timeout_terminates_descendant_processes` asked the filesystem a question the filesystem cannot answer: `descendant-survived` is absent both when the descendant died and when it is alive but still sleeping, so on a loaded macOS runner the old 150 ms proof-of-life lost its race with the kill (run 32272689475, job 96137354605). The fixture now records the descendant's pid and the test polls the kernel for it, naming each failure separately: never spawned, still running, or finished before the kill arrived. Verified by mutation -- a descendant moved into its own process group is reported as still running. See finding 15. |
| R1021-30 | A deadline a CI script depends on exists on every runner the tests run on. | `scripts/apt-install-with-retry.sh` bounded its attempts with GNU `timeout`, which macOS does not ship, so the macOS core slices failed the tests that drive it while the Linux job it ships in was green (run 32282461075, jobs 96170638546 and 96170638704). `scripts/run-with-deadline.sh` is one deadline for both families, keeping `timeout`'s 124-on-expiry contract, and `no_committed_script_reaches_for_a_timeout_binary_macos_does_not_have` holds the rule for every tracked script and workflow rather than for the line that was caught. Writing the deadline means owning its accuracy too: it is never early, which `the_deadline_never_expires_before_the_time_it_was_given` pins after the first draft expired a 3s deadline in 2.6s. Both families now run it: every `ci_cd::issue_1021` test is green on the macOS core slices of run 32294252392. See findings 16, 17 and 18. |
| R1021-31 | A request that names code as the artefact and names nothing else is a coding request, not a web search. | `write_program_parameters` decides it by subtraction: everything the lexicon can account for -- the asking verb, the artefact noun, and the closed-class words a request is built out of (the new `request_function_word` role) -- is removed from the prompt, and the route fires only when nothing is left. `мне нужен код` therefore reaches the honest dead end that asks which language, worded in the language it was asked in (`a_coding_request_naming_no_language_is_a_coding_request`, `the_languageless_coding_request_is_answered_in_its_own_language`), and the asking verb generalizes to every other one and every supported language (`asking_for_code_is_a_coding_request_whatever_the_asking_verb`). Because the test is *nothing else was named*, `give me the code of this repository` and `I need a code review` still belong to whichever route owns the subject they name (`an_asking_verb_alone_is_not_a_coding_request`). |
| R1021-32 | #824/#944: a move is *performed and verified*, not issued. | A command that changes the workspace is carried out as the ordered recipe its seed intent declares -- preconditions, preparation, the action, postconditions -- with each step observed before the next is planned (`src/agentic_coding/mutating_action.rs`). The predicates are data: `data/seed/shell-intents.lino` gives `mv` and `cp` an `effect` block, which is why `cp` is carried out the same way without `cp` appearing anywhere in `src/`, and why the held-out ladder rung `824.L5` passes. A deep destination works because the recipe prepares the destination's parent (`824.L4`); an occupied destination stops the recipe before the action and is reported as the check that stopped it and the status it exited with, rather than as the completion `mv`'s own exit code would have suggested (`824.L2`, `a_move_onto_an_occupied_destination_stops_before_it_acts`). |
| R1021-33 | Every dependency is on its newest release that builds on stable Rust, and the crate is on the current edition. | The seven real manifests are refreshed together, and they are the seven `git ls-files` finds: `Cargo.toml` (31 direct crates, with `link-cli` owning the native doublets/file-mapping stack) with `Cargo.lock`, and the six `package.json` files -- root (with `bun.lock`), `desktop/`, `vscode/`, `tests/e2e/`, `experiments/agent_cli_e2e/issue_819_tui/` (with its own `bun.lock`) and `experiments/opencode_vscode_e2e/driver/`, the last of which declares no versioned dependency to refresh. `experiments/agentic_cli_matrix/clients.lock` pins CLI clients rather than packages and is refreshed alongside them. The `package.json` files under `dev/log/` and `docs/case-studies/` are archived copies kept as evidence of what a run saw, and are deliberately left untouched. Six crates needed more than a version number, and the code moved rather than the requirement: `sha2` 0.11 returns a digest type without `LowerHex`, so the nine places that rendered a digest by hand now go through `source_fetch::hex_lower` (finding 28). The crate is on edition 2024, which `build.rs` exports so the `rustc` that judges a self-authored version compiles the same language (`the_crate_is_on_edition_2024_and_the_judge_compiles_the_same_edition`). Stable-only was a rule with no gate behind it and now has one: `nothing_in_the_tree_reaches_for_a_nightly_toolchain` refuses a toolchain file, a toolchain action asking for anything but stable, a per-invocation override, a bootstrap variable, and an unstable feature attribute, across every tracked source, script and workflow. Two crates stay where they are on purpose and say why: `command-stream` at the `=0.16.0` issue #1014 pinned, and `@openai/codex` at 0.147.0 while openai/codex#39487 is open. Five lockfile duplicates are inherited from crates that have not published against the newer major, named one by one in finding 29. |
| R1021-34 | A gate that reports a failure names the thing that failed, not the healthy things beside it. | The `Broken Link Checker` failed three times over links that answer 200, because `extractBrokenUrls` in `scripts/check-web-archive.mjs` located the failing part of lychee's report by searching for one hard-coded `## Errors per input` heading. lychee writes only the sections a run has links for, so a report whose sole failure was a timeout matched nothing and fell back to parsing the whole document, harvesting every healthy redirect in it. Sections are now sliced out by heading and a section counts as failing unless its category is one of the outcomes known to be healthy -- selection by exclusion, so an unrecognised future category is reported rather than silently dropped, because a false positive is loud and a dropped failure is not. The four tests added to `scripts/check-web-archive.test.mjs` cover the shapes the old lookup got wrong (`reports a timeout when the report has no errors section`, `collects failures from every failing section, not just the first`, `treats an unrecognised section as failing`, `ignores the summary table and the healthy sections around it`) and all four fail against the previous parser; `.github/workflows/links.yml` already ran them ahead of lychee, and missed the defect only because every earlier test described a report that has an errors section. The real report from run 32454084765 is kept as a fixture and replayed by `experiments/issue-1021-link-checker-false-positive/reproduce.mjs`. What stays a finding rather than a change: the job still fails whenever lychee exits non-zero, so a lone runner-side timeout reds the gate over a healthy link, and making that non-fatal would be moving a limit. See finding 32. |
| R1021-35 | Refreshing a pinned client is finished when its leg is green, not when the version number changes. | The `clients.lock` refresh in this branch reddened two Agentic CLI Matrix legs, and both were root-caused rather than pinned back. `t3code` 0.0.33 grew `pair` and `service`, which the leg's verbatim `--help` assertion caught by design; neither is a prompt path -- one mints a token for an already-running server, one manages a background daemon -- so the contract is re-recorded in `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` and the tripwire stays exact. `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` 2.1.238 added a once-per-session connection warm-up, `HEAD $ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/api/hello` behind `providerCache.preconnectFired`, which reaches our wrapper's base URL as `/api/anthropic/api/hello`; the doubled `/api` is nobody's defect, since `https://api.anthropic.com/api/hello` answers `200 {"message": "hello"}` to `GET` and `200` with an empty body to `HEAD` without credentials. An Anthropic-compatible surface answers it too, so `src/server.rs` serves both spellings and `matrix_assert_proxy_ok` is left alone -- the same fix issue #671 made for the bare base path, for the same reason. `tests/integration/issue_1021_client_preflight.rs` pins all three probes and was falsified against the unpatched server. See finding 33. |
| R1021-36 | A step that is terminated for running too long reports what made it slow. | `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh` announces the failure, so it is what asks the question a reader asks next. At the two moments a budget is in trouble -- the 70% warning and the termination -- it prints sccache's own counters, and only when `RUSTC_WRAPPER` names sccache, so a budgeted step that compiles nothing stays exactly as quiet as before (`a_budget_that_expires_reports_the_compiler_cache_counters`, `a_budget_warning_reports_the_counters_without_touching_the_result`, `a_budget_that_wraps_no_compiler_reports_no_counters`; the first two fail against the previous script). This is the standing debug-output clause applied to CI: `Test (macos-15-intel / specification)` was terminated at its full 1200s budget still compiling dependencies, and the two candidate causes -- a slower runner, a colder compiler cache -- leave the same trace in the log, because cargo prints `Running \`sccache rustc ...\`` on a hit exactly as it does on a miss. Narrowing them took reconstructing per-crate rustc timestamps out of a megabyte of raw job log, and even that only ruled out a *partial* cache difference rather than closing the question, because the counters that would close it were never printed. The budget itself was not moved. See finding 34. |
| R1021-37 | A name is part of the interface, and a static analyser reads it as one. | The `CodeQL` check reported 99 critical and high alerts on this branch, and every one of them was produced by an identifier's spelling. `rust/hard-coded-cryptographic-value` makes a sink of any argument reaching a parameter literally named `password`, `iv`, `nonce` or `salt`, so the `salt` parameter of `sample_index` -- an FNV-1a draw with no cryptography anywhere near it -- reported the 98 `temperature`, `guess_probability` and `questioning_rigor` literals that 24 files write into a `FormalizationSelectionConfig`; `rust/cleartext-logging` reads `session.?(id|key)` as account information, so `src/cli_improve.rs` printing FNV-1a digests out of a binding called `session_id` reported as a leaked session token. The values are renamed after what they are (`seed`, `agent_session_digests`) with every seed string and every digest byte-identical before and after, and `tests/unit/ci-cd/codeql_sink_heuristics.rs` holds both heuristics over every Rust file CodeQL analyses rather than over the two sites that were caught -- the same file set, minus the prefixes `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` ignores, which `the_scan_skips_the_same_directories_the_codeql_config_ignores` keeps in step. What stays a finding rather than a change: the two `assert!` alerts in `tests/unit/docs_requirements_issue_917.rs` and `_918.rs` are true positives over real Agent CLI session ids and are left open rather than spelled around or dismissed, and `salt`'s presence in the upstream sink list -- where `key` is already excluded as too false-positive prone -- is proposed as an upstream report rather than filed. See finding 36. |

## Issue #1073 Reasoning Standard: Unconditional Depth, Refutation First, Computed Trust

Issue [#1073](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1073) takes one
reference dialog -- a disk-space cleanup session -- and makes the properties that
made it good the *floor* rather than the ceiling. The instruction that governs
every row below is the one attached to that goal: the floor holds for the trivial
request too, and it is never conditional on being asked. See
`docs/case-studies/issue-1073/` for the case study and the contradiction audit.

The standard is data. `data/meta/reasoning-standard.lino` declares seven gates
(order, trigger, requirement, the reference behaviour it was adopted from, the
slug it reports on failure) and five numeric thresholds with the reason each
number is what it is; `src/reasoning_standard/` loads it and evaluates every gate
as a pure predicate over a `ReasoningEpisode`. Nothing on that path consults a
model.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1073-1 | Deep reasoning everywhere: the reference depth is the floor, applies to trivial requests, and is never conditional on task difficulty or on prompting. | Three defaults moved from the quiet setting to the full one: `RecursionMode::Down` -> `Both`, `SelectionMode::Off` -> `Record`, `SkillMode::Off` -> `Accumulate`, each reachable before only through `SolverConfig` or a `FORMAL_AI_*` variable. The reasoning-standard audit itself takes no mode at all: `record_meta_core` calls it unconditionally, and `the_meta_core_runs_the_audit_with_no_mode_in_front_of_it` fails if a condition is ever put in front of it. `open_episode` opens an episode from the formalization alone, so the greeting `hi` gets the same seven-gate ledger the reference dialog gets: `instruction_formalization` reports `Violated` with `courtesy:no_instructions_gathered` and `instruction_sources:0:required:2`, the other six report `NotTriggered` naming the trigger that was false, and the verdict is `not_confirmed_not_refuted` with its blockers named. The obligations are enumerated identically either way (`depth_floor_enumerates_every_gate_even_for_a_trivial_episode`, `the_depth_floor_holds_for_the_smallest_request_the_pipeline_can_formalize`, measured in `docs/case-studies/issue-1073/logs/reasoning-standard-audit.log`). |
| R1073-2 | Instructions for the task class are gathered and *formalized* into machine-checkable instruction sets, not paraphrased. | `src/reasoning_standard/instructions.rs` compiles gathered steps into an ordered set in which every step carries a check; a step with an empty check is unverifiable and fails the `instruction_formalization` gate. The set must draw on at least `minimum_instruction_sources` (2) distinct sources before a step counts as corroborated, since a single source cannot corroborate itself (`gathered_instructions_are_compiled_into_checkable_steps`). |
| R1073-3 | Official documentation and trustworthy sources are consulted as a default step of reasoning, not as an escalation. | The `documentation_default` gate fires whenever any source was consulted and requires at least `minimum_documentation_sources` (1) of them to be primary for its subject -- the subject speaking about itself, or a first-hand record of it (`primary_documentation_is_required_by_default`). |
| R1073-4 | Source trust is computed from proximity to primary sources, never assumed; conflicts resolve toward the more primary source. | `PrimacyChain::derive_trust` derives the tier from the chain's structure alone: an empty chain is `Unoriginal` for `NoPrimacyChain`, a hop that cannot name its upstream is `Unoriginal` for `UnfoundedStep`, distance zero is first-party or first-hand journalism, and a named upstream chain is independent corroboration. `resolve_conflict` prefers the shorter distance and answers `Unresolved` at equal distance rather than picking a side. The live registry is held to the same rule: every source in `data/seed/sources-registry.lino` declares a `primacy` chain citing the site's own policy, `SourceRecord::tier` is the derived value, `tier_from_seed` and its silent `_ => independent_corroboration` arm are deleted, and the hand-written tier survives only as `asserted_tier`, checked against the derivation (`source_trust_is_derived_from_the_primacy_chain`). |
| R1073-5 | Refutation first, with deliberate variety; only refuted refutations or a positively proven alternative permit leaning toward a conclusion, otherwise "not confirmed and not refuted" with the blockers named. | The `refutation_variety` gate requires `minimum_refutation_attempts` (3) attempts with *distinct mechanisms* spanning `minimum_refutation_axis_kinds` (2) of the three kinds -- a different mechanism, a different source, a different denied assumption -- so three restatements of one doubt count as one. `Verdict::NotConfirmedNotRefuted` carries `blockers()`: the gates that failed and the checks that could not be run. It is the honest default, not a fallback (`conclusions_need_varied_refutations_before_they_may_be_leaned_toward`). |
| R1073-6 | Requirements 1-5 are formal checkable procedures, so the same conclusions stay reachable with the LLM removed. | Every gate is a pure predicate over the episode record; `audit` reaches its verdict with no model in the loop, and `the_standard_is_a_formal_procedure_that_replays_without_a_model` replays the same episode to the same verdict and the same event payloads. The procedure is itself data: `data/meta/reasoning-standard-recipe.lino` declares the eight steps, the seven gates and the nine implementing functions, and `tests/unit/specification/reasoning_standard_meta_algorithm.rs` fails when the recipe and the source disagree. |
| R1073-7 | Contradiction audit: enumerate what defines reasoning today, flag assumed trust, single-source conclusions and conditional depth, update each flagged place, and leave a regression derived from the reference dialog. | `docs/case-studies/issue-1073/contradiction-audit.md` is the enumeration and the disposition of each finding, including the two places deliberately left unchanged and why. The regression is `data/meta/reasoning-standard-reference-episode.lino` -- the reference dialog with its project-specific tooling, absolute paths and session management dropped -- which clears all seven gates, together with the mutation set in `tests/unit/issue_1073_reasoning_standard.rs` that makes each gate fail when the behaviour it enforces is removed. |

## Standing Doctrine: Compiled Logic, Interfacing-Only JavaScript (2026-08-04)

Stated by the project owner as a standing architectural requirement; it
strengthens R194/R249/R380 from "as much as possible" to a boundary rule.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R536 | JavaScript must be used only as interfacing glue and for JSX (React) UI components. All logic must be compiled Rust — native on the server side, WebAssembly in the web app — and the same WASM web engine must be reused by the desktop shell and other surfaces (VS Code, etc.) rather than reimplemented. | Partially implemented: `src/web/wasm-worker/` owns the parity-sensitive primitives and `src/web/app/main.jsx` is the JSX UI; `src/web/worker/*.js` still carries ~27,700 lines of mirrored solver logic under the shrink-only ratchet `scripts/check-worker-line-budget.rs`. Desktop serves the same `src/web/` engine bundle and prefers the native `formal-ai serve` process; the VS Code web host runs the in-process WASM engine. Full absorption of the JS worker into Rust→WASM is tracked by [#658](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/658) (R380); after absorption the JavaScript surface is capped and lint-enforced as UI/glue. |
